transcript.text: Bit of a weird one - my son put the microwave on for 10 minutes with nothing in it by accident. Now there's a horrible smell. Is it broken?

It may not be permanently broken, but running a microwave empty for 10 minutes can overheat and damage the magnetron (the part that makes the microwaves) or other internal components. A burning/plastic/electrical smell is a warning sign.

1. Switch it off and unplug it. Open windows/ventilate the room.
2. Let it cool completely — at least 30–60 minutes.
3. Check the inside for obvious scorching, melted plastic, damage to the waveguide cover (usually a small cardboard-like panel on an inside wall), or any smoke residue.
4. Do not take the casing off — microwaves contain high-voltage components that can remain dangerous even unplugged.

If, once cool, there is still a strong electrical/burning smell, visible damage, sparking, buzzing/crackling, smoke, or it trips the electrics, don’t use it again: arrange a repair/replacement.

If there’s no visible damage and the smell largely clears, you can cautiously test it by heating a microwave-safe mug/bowl of water for about one minute — never empty. If the water doesn’t get hot, it makes unusual noises, or the smell returns, stop using it and have it checked.

Ten minutes empty is long enough that I’d lean toward having it inspected or replacing it if it’s an older/cheap unit, especially given the “horrible” smell.

Thanks. It's turned off at the switch but still plugged in. There was some smoke coming out of the vents at the side when we stopped it, and there's a brownish mark on the side panel inside. Smell is fading but still there. Is it safe, or should I just bin it?

With smoke from the vents and a brown/scorched mark inside, do not use it again. Treat it as damaged.

• Unplug it from the wall (switching off at the socket is good, but unplugging removes any doubt), if it’s safe to reach the plug.
• Leave the door shut/avoid handling it until fully cool and the smell has dispersed. Ventilate the room.
• Don’t try the “mug of water” test, don’t run it again, and don’t remove the outer casing. The brown mark may be a burned waveguide cover or internal wall damage, and smoke suggests overheating/arcing.
• If it is still smoking, gets hot again while switched off, or you see flames, move people away and call the fire service. Don’t use water on an electrical appliance.

In practical terms, after 10 minutes empty plus smoke and scorching, replacement is usually the sensible option unless it is a valuable model and you want a qualified microwave repair technician to inspect it. Microwaves have hazardous high-voltage components even after being unplugged, so it’s not a DIY repair.

Don’t put it in the normal household bin: take it to an electrical/WEEE recycling point or arrange retailer/local-authority electrical appliance collection.
